stages.name: Foundations
stages.summary: Numbers, the four operations, fractions, decimals, percent and ratio.

stages.name: Pre-algebra
stages.summary: Number theory, integers, exponents, order of operations, first equations.

topics.title: Counting and numbers to 20
objectives: Count objects up to 20 and say how many
Read and write numerals 0 to 20
Explain that zero means none
misconceptions: Counting an object twice or skipping one
Thinking the last number said is just a label, not the total

topics.title: Numbers to 100: tens and ones
objectives: Group objects into tens and ones
Read and write two-digit numbers
Say the value of each digit in a two-digit number
misconceptions: Writing 'forty-six' as 406
Thinking the 4 in 46 means four, not forty

topics.title: Comparing and ordering numbers
objectives: Use <, > and = correctly
Place numbers on a number line
Arrange a set of numbers in ascending and descending order
misconceptions: Comparing by the last digit instead of the first
Reading the < sign backwards

topics.title: Place value to thousands
objectives: Read and write numbers up to 9,999
Write a number in expanded form (3,405 = 3000 + 400 + 5)
Explain why zero is needed as a placeholder
misconceptions: Dropping the zero in 3,405 and writing 345
Thinking a digit has the same value in every position

topics.title: Large numbers: lakh and crore
objectives: Read and write numbers up to 99,99,99,999 using the Indian system
Place commas correctly in the Indian system
Write a large number in words
misconceptions: Using groups of three digits throughout (1,000,000 instead of 10,00,000)
Thinking one lakh is 1,000,000
topics.indian_context: Population of cities, prices of houses, cricket stadium capacities.

topics.title: Million and billion: two ways to write big numbers
objectives: Read and write numbers using million and billion
Convert between lakh/crore and million/billion
Place commas correctly in the international system
misconceptions: Thinking 1 crore equals 1 million
Mixing the two comma systems in one number

topics.title: Rounding and estimation
objectives: Round numbers to the nearest 10, 100 and 1,000
Estimate a sum or difference by rounding first
Judge whether an answer is reasonable
misconceptions: Rounding 45 down to 40
Changing every digit after the rounding place to 9 instead of 0

topics.title: What addition means
objectives: Model addition as putting groups together
Recall addition facts up to 20
Explain that order does not change a sum
misconceptions: Counting the starting number again when counting on
Thinking 3 + 5 and 5 + 3 give different answers

topics.title: What subtraction means
objectives: Model subtraction as taking away and as finding a difference
Use addition facts to check subtraction
Explain why order matters in subtraction
misconceptions: Thinking 3 − 5 is the same as 5 − 3
Believing subtraction always means 'take away' only

topics.title: Adding and subtracting with regrouping
objectives: Add two-digit numbers with carrying
Subtract two-digit numbers with borrowing
Explain carrying as trading 10 ones for 1 ten
misconceptions: Subtracting the smaller digit from the larger in each column (52 − 27 = 35)
Forgetting to add the carried ten

topics.title: Adding and subtracting large numbers
objectives: Add and subtract numbers up to 6 digits in columns
Borrow across zeros (5,000 − 1,248)
Check a subtraction by adding
misconceptions: Misaligning digits when numbers have different lengths
Borrowing across zeros incorrectly

topics.title: Multiplication as equal groups
objectives: Model multiplication as equal groups and as arrays
Write repeated addition as multiplication
Explain why 3 × 4 = 4 × 3 using an array
misconceptions: Thinking multiplication always makes a number bigger
Adding instead of multiplying (3 × 4 = 7)

topics.title: Times tables to 10 × 10
objectives: Recall multiplication facts up to 10 × 10
Use known facts to work out unknown ones (7 × 8 from 7 × 4)
Multiply by 0 and 1 correctly
misconceptions: Thinking any number times 0 is that number
Memorising tables without seeing patterns

topics.title: Division as sharing and grouping
objectives: Model division as fair sharing and as grouping
Use multiplication facts to divide
Find and interpret a remainder
misconceptions: Thinking 6 ÷ 2 equals 2 ÷ 6
Leaving a remainder larger than the divisor

topics.title: Multiplying larger numbers
objectives: Multiply by 10, 100 and 1,000
Multiply a multi-digit number by a one-digit number
Multiply two two-digit numbers using the column method
misconceptions: Forgetting the placeholder zero in the second row
Thinking 'add a zero' works for decimals too

topics.title: Long division
objectives: Divide a multi-digit number by a one-digit number
Divide by a two-digit number
Check division using multiplication and the remainder
misconceptions: Skipping a zero in the quotient (1,224 ÷ 12 = 12)
Bringing down two digits at once

topics.title: Choosing the operation: word problems
objectives: Decide which operation a word problem needs
Solve two-step word problems
Check that an answer makes sense in the story
misconceptions: Choosing an operation from keywords alone ('more' always means add)
Ignoring what the remainder means in the story
topics.indian_context: Train tickets, sharing laddoos, market shopping, school trip budgets.

topics.title: Factors and multiples
objectives: List all factors of a number up to 100
List the first multiples of a number
Find common factors and common multiples by listing
misconceptions: Confusing factors with multiples
Forgetting 1 and the number itself as factors

topics.title: Fractions as equal parts
objectives: Name a fraction from a shape divided into equal parts
Explain what the numerator and denominator mean
Find a fraction of a small quantity (1/3 of 12)
misconceptions: Accepting unequal parts as 'quarters'
Thinking a bigger denominator means a bigger fraction
topics.indian_context: Sharing a roti or a pizza, slices of a watermelon.

topics.title: Fractions on a number line
objectives: Place fractions between 0 and 1 on a number line
Place fractions greater than 1 on a number line
Explain that a fraction is a number, not just a shape
misconceptions: Counting tick marks instead of spaces
Thinking fractions can only be less than 1

topics.title: Equivalent fractions
objectives: Show two fractions are equal using diagrams and the number line
Make equivalent fractions by multiplying or dividing top and bottom
Write a fraction in its simplest form
misconceptions: Adding the same number to top and bottom (1/2 = 2/3)
Thinking 2/4 is bigger than 1/2 because the numbers are bigger

topics.title: Comparing fractions
objectives: Compare fractions with the same denominator or the same numerator
Compare any two fractions using a common denominator
Order a set of fractions
misconceptions: Thinking 1/8 > 1/4 because 8 > 4
Comparing only numerators when denominators differ

topics.title: Improper fractions and mixed numbers
objectives: Convert an improper fraction to a mixed number
Convert a mixed number to an improper fraction
Place mixed numbers on a number line
misconceptions: Writing 2 1/3 as 3/3
Thinking an improper fraction is 'wrong'

topics.title: Adding and subtracting fractions with the same denominator
objectives: Add and subtract fractions with the same denominator
Explain why the denominator stays the same
Give answers greater than 1 as mixed numbers
misconceptions: Adding denominators too (1/5 + 2/5 = 3/10)

topics.title: Adding and subtracting fractions with different denominators
objectives: Find a common denominator
Add and subtract fractions with different denominators
Add and subtract mixed numbers
misconceptions: Adding tops and bottoms separately (1/2 + 1/3 = 2/5)
Changing the denominator without changing the numerator

topics.title: Multiplying fractions
objectives: Find a fraction of a whole number
Multiply two fractions and explain it with an area model
Multiply mixed numbers
misconceptions: Thinking multiplying always makes a number bigger
Multiplying the whole parts and fraction parts of mixed numbers separately

topics.title: Dividing fractions
objectives: Explain division by a fraction as 'how many fit into'
Divide using the reciprocal
Solve sharing problems involving fractions
misconceptions: Flipping the first fraction instead of the second
Thinking dividing always makes a number smaller

topics.title: Decimals: tenths and hundredths
objectives: Read and write tenths, hundredths and thousandths
Connect decimals to fractions with denominators 10, 100, 1000
Use decimals for rupees and paise, metres and centimetres
misconceptions: Thinking 0.25 is bigger than 0.3 because 25 > 3
Reading 0.05 as 'zero point five'

topics.title: Comparing and rounding decimals
objectives: Compare and order decimals
Place decimals on a number line
Round decimals to a given number of places
misconceptions: Thinking longer decimals are always bigger
Ignoring the place value of the digits after the point

topics.title: Adding and subtracting decimals
objectives: Line up decimal points to add and subtract
Use zeros to fill empty places
Solve money problems with rupees and paise
misconceptions: Lining up the last digits instead of the decimal points

topics.title: Multiplying and dividing decimals
objectives: Multiply and divide decimals by 10, 100 and 1,000
Multiply a decimal by a decimal
Divide a decimal by a whole number and by a decimal
misconceptions: Keeping the decimal point in the same place after multiplying by 10
Placing the decimal point by counting from the left

topics.title: Converting between fractions and decimals
objectives: Convert a decimal to a fraction in simplest form
Convert a fraction to a decimal by division
Recognise recurring decimals such as 1/3 = 0.333…
misconceptions: Writing 1/4 as 1.4
Thinking 0.333… is exactly equal to 0.33

topics.title: Percent means 'out of 100'
objectives: Explain percent as a fraction out of 100
Convert between percents, fractions and decimals
Recognise common benchmarks (50%, 25%, 10%, 1%)
misconceptions: Thinking a percent cannot be more than 100
Writing 5% as 0.5

topics.title: Finding a percentage of an amount
objectives: Find a percentage of an amount using 10% and 1% steps
Find a percentage of an amount by multiplication
Express one quantity as a percentage of another
misconceptions: Finding 20% by dividing by 20
Using the wrong whole when expressing as a percentage

topics.title: Discounts, GST and percentage change
objectives: Calculate a price after a discount
Calculate a price after adding GST
Find the percentage increase or decrease between two values
misconceptions: Thinking a 20% rise then a 20% fall returns to the start
Dividing by the new value instead of the original
topics.indian_context: Festival-sale discounts, GST on a bill, rise in petrol prices.

topics.title: Ratio
objectives: Write a ratio to compare two quantities
Simplify a ratio
Share an amount in a given ratio
misconceptions: Treating 2:3 as 2/3 of the whole instead of 2 parts out of 5
Writing a ratio in the wrong order
topics.indian_context: Mixing rice and dal, sharing prize money, recipe ingredients.

topics.title: Proportion and the unitary method
objectives: Use the unitary method to find the cost of many from the cost of one
Decide whether two quantities are in proportion
Solve rate problems (speed, price per kg)
misconceptions: Using addition instead of multiplication to scale up
Assuming every relationship is proportional

topics.title: Divisibility rules
objectives: Test divisibility by 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 9 and 10
Explain why the rule for 3 works
Use divisibility rules to find factors quickly
misconceptions: Using the digit-sum rule for 4
Thinking a number divisible by 2 and 4 must be divisible by 8

topics.title: Prime and composite numbers
objectives: Define prime and composite numbers
Find primes up to 100 with the Sieve of Eratosthenes
Explain why 1 is neither prime nor composite
misconceptions: Thinking all odd numbers are prime
Thinking 1 is prime

topics.title: Prime factorisation
objectives: Write a number as a product of primes using a factor tree
Use repeated division to factorise
Explain why every number has exactly one prime factorisation
misconceptions: Stopping at a composite factor
Thinking different factor trees give different answers

topics.title: HCF and LCM
objectives: Find the HCF of two or three numbers
Find the LCM of two or three numbers
Choose HCF or LCM to solve a word problem
Use HCF × LCM = product of two numbers
misconceptions: Confusing HCF and LCM
Thinking the LCM is always the product of the numbers
topics.indian_context: Bells ringing together at a temple, cutting cloth into equal pieces.

topics.title: Negative numbers and integers
objectives: Place negative numbers on a number line
Compare and order integers
Use integers for temperature, height above sea level, and money owed
misconceptions: Thinking −8 is greater than −3
Thinking negative numbers are not real numbers
topics.indian_context: Winter temperatures in Leh, depth below sea level, a shopkeeper's credit.

topics.title: Adding and subtracting integers
objectives: Add integers using a number line
Subtract an integer by adding its opposite
Solve problems involving changes in temperature or money
misconceptions: Thinking subtracting a negative makes the number smaller
Applying 'two negatives make a positive' to addition

topics.title: Multiplying and dividing integers
objectives: Multiply and divide integers with the correct sign
Explain why a negative times a negative is positive using patterns
Evaluate products with several negative factors
misconceptions: Getting the sign right but forgetting it in the final answer

topics.title: Powers and exponents
objectives: Write repeated multiplication using exponents
Evaluate powers with whole-number exponents
Explain why any non-zero number to the power 0 is 1
misconceptions: Thinking 3² = 6
Thinking 5⁰ = 0

topics.title: Squares and square roots
objectives: Recognise perfect squares up to 400
Find square roots of perfect squares using prime factorisation
Estimate the square root of a non-square number between two whole numbers
misconceptions: Thinking the square root of 16 is 8
Thinking square roots of non-squares do not exist

topics.title: Order of operations (BODMAS)
objectives: Evaluate expressions using the correct order of operations
Explain that division and multiplication (and addition and subtraction) go left to right
Use brackets to change the order
misconceptions: Always doing division before multiplication because D comes before M
Working strictly left to right for everything

topics.title: Laws of exponents
objectives: Multiply and divide powers with the same base
Raise a power to a power
Evaluate negative exponents as reciprocals
misconceptions: Multiplying exponents when multiplying powers (2³ × 2⁴ = 2¹²)
Thinking 2⁻³ is negative

topics.title: Very large and very small numbers
objectives: Write numbers in standard form (scientific notation)
Convert from standard form to ordinary numbers
Compare numbers written in standard form
misconceptions: Writing 45 × 10³ as standard form
Moving the decimal point the wrong way for small numbers
topics.indian_context: Distance to the Moon for Chandrayaan, India's population, size of a bacterium.

topics.title: Rational numbers
objectives: Define a rational number as p/q with q ≠ 0
Place negative fractions on a number line
Add, subtract, multiply and divide rational numbers
misconceptions: Thinking −1/2 and 1/−2 are different numbers
Thinking integers are not rational numbers

topics.title: Letters for numbers: variables and expressions
objectives: Use a letter to stand for an unknown or varying number
Write an expression from a word description
Understand 3n as 3 × n
misconceptions: Thinking a letter stands for an object ('a' means apples)
Thinking 3n means thirty-something

topics.title: Evaluating expressions
objectives: Substitute values into an expression
Evaluate expressions with negative and fractional values
Use a formula (perimeter, cost) by substitution
misconceptions: Substituting −3 into x² as −9
Writing 2x with x = 5 as 25

topics.title: Simplifying expressions: like terms and brackets
objectives: Collect like terms
Expand brackets using the distributive property
Simplify expressions that need both
misconceptions: Combining unlike terms (2x + 3y = 5xy)
Multiplying only the first term inside the bracket

topics.title: Solving one-step equations
objectives: Explain an equation as a balance
Solve equations of the form x + a = b and ax = b
Check a solution by substituting it back
misconceptions: Doing an operation to one side only
Thinking x always has to be a whole number

topics.title: Solving two-step equations
objectives: Solve equations of the form ax + b = c
Solve equations with the variable on both sides
Solve equations that need brackets expanded first
misconceptions: Undoing operations in the wrong order
Changing the sign of a term without moving it across

topics.title: Writing and solving equations from stories
objectives: Define a variable for the unknown in a story
Write an equation from a word problem
Solve it and interpret the answer in the story
misconceptions: Writing the equation in the order the words appear
Forgetting to answer the question that was asked

topics.title: Number patterns and rules
objectives: Continue a number or shape pattern
Find the rule for the nth term of a linear pattern
Use the rule to find any term
misconceptions: Only finding the term-to-term rule (add 3) and not the position rule (3n + 1)

topics.title: Simple interest
objectives: Explain principal, rate, time and interest
Calculate simple interest using I = PRT/100
Find the total amount repaid or received
misconceptions: Forgetting to convert months into years
Adding interest to the rate instead of the amount
topics.indian_context: A fixed deposit at a bank or post office, a loan for a bicycle.
